title: Time Jump — 10:00 AM

fields.narration: It is now 10:00. The yellow-green cloud over Rail Spot 2 has grown visibly larger, and the fence-line detector AT-905 has just alarmed. The release continues at roughly 40 lb a minute, and the plume is drifting east toward the Riverside Addition and Corbin Falls Elementary School. The ERT is now in Level A suits and en route to the loading rack. The shift cannot confirm the status of ESD-310 or the hand valve at Rail Spot 2 from the control room screen.
worldState: The plume from Rail Spot 2 is now visible from the Administration Building and the east fence line.
AT-905 (Riverside Addition east fence) has alarmed at 1.3 ppm.
The ERT is en route to Rail Spot 2 in Level A suits and has activated their HAZMAT alert on the site radio.
The DeltaV HMI continues to show ESD-310 closed and WT-302 at 38.1 tons, but field verification is impossible due to the active vapor plume and lack of real-time video feed from the spot.
The wind remains from the west-south-west at 6 mph, per WX-1.
The EHS Manager has completed the initial plume model using EPA/NOAA ALOHA and is preparing a threat-zone map for the Incident Commander.
The community alert via CAER-Text has been triggered for E-1 and E-2 sectors.
fields.facilitatorNote: This is a time jump to establish physical escalation and urgency. The Incident Commander must now decide whether to declare a General Emergency based on the AT-905 alarm and ERT presence. The OT Engineer should begin forensic review of TS-EWS-01.
